transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Yes, that's very normal, especially for a Bosch. Wet plastics are the number one complaint with them, and it's down to how they dry rather than a fault.

## Why it happens

Most Bosch dishwashers, including the Serie 4, use condensation drying rather than a heating element blowing hot air. The final rinse heats everything up, and moisture is meant to evaporate off the hot dishes and condense on the cooler stainless steel walls.

That works well for ceramics and glass, which hold heat. Plastic holds very little heat, so it cools quickly and water stays sitting on it. Tubs with recessed bases that collect water are the worst. Drips on glasses usually come from water rolling off the rack or from upturned bases of items above.

## Things that help (roughly in order of impact)

1. Use rinse aid, and turn it up. This makes the biggest difference. Rinse aid helps water sheet off rather than bead. Don't rely on all-in-one tablets for this. Fill the separate rinse aid compartment anyway. The dosage is adjustable (usually levels 0–6 in the settings menu; check your manual), so try raising it a notch or two.
2. Use the Extra Dry / drying option if your model has it. It raises the final rinse temperature.
3. Avoid Eco for loads with lots of plastic. Eco runs cooler, so drying is weaker. Auto or Intensive will dry better (though Eco is genuinely more efficient for everyday loads).
4. Crack the door open after the cycle finishes. Some Bosch models do this automatically (look for "EfficientDry" or "Auto Open Dry"). If yours doesn't, opening it a few inches for 15–30 minutes lets the steam escape.
5. Unload the bottom rack first so water pooled on the top rack doesn't drip down onto dry items.
6. Load plastics at an angle on the top rack so water runs off rather than pooling in hollows.
7. Keep the salt topped up if you're in a hard water area, as limescale also hurts drying.

## When it might actually be a fault

It's worth investigating if:
• Everything comes out soaking, including plates and mugs
• Dishes feel cold or barely warm straight after a normal cycle (could indicate a heating problem)
• There's standing water in the bottom of the machine (drainage issue, so check the filter first)

If it's mainly plastics and a few drips, that's just the nature of the beast, and rinse aid plus opening the door will get you most of the way there.
